summary: Ferry County tower built 1931 on the Colville Reservation; register says staffed most summers, one site says recently abandoned; permit needed for non-tribal visitors.

facts.design: 45-foot steel Aermotor tower; frame cabin below the summit
facts.agency: Colville Indian Reservation (administers); Colville National Forest (cooperator)

staffing.status: disputed: register and firelookout.com say staffed most summers; Willhite site says it appears recently abandoned

access.note: On tribal land. Non-tribal visitors need a recreation permit; a trip guide updated March 2026 gives $80 a year. Ask the Colville Tribes before going.

visit.trail_note: Road reaches near the summit; the final stretch is steep, rocky and rough, with a parking area before the worst of it (TrailChick: most people park and hike the last mile)

events.note: Register: built 1931 as a 45-foot steel Aermotor tower. Willhite: an inscription inside says the tower was finished June 19, 1931 at 11 a.m.
Wenatchee Daily World, September 14, 1931: Cody Butte and Lynx Creek lookouts relieved after Saturday night's rain
July 12, 1932 item names James Someday at the Cody Butte station
July 17, 1943 Colville Examiner names Miss Ellen Adams, Mason City, on Cody Butte; teachers hired as summer fire lookouts on the Colville National Forest
Registered April 11, 2022 as US 1523, WA 72; nominated by Christine Estrada

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 4,766 ft (1,453 m); firelookout.com and TrailChick give 4,764 ft. The record keeps the register's coordinates and 1452.7 m. The two-foot gap is noted, not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Current use is disputed and not resolved: the register text (undated, also on firelookout.com) says staffed most summers; the Willhite page (undated text, photo captions 1934 and 2016) says it appears recently abandoned; TrailChick (visited May 2019) does not say. Check with the Colville Tribes before publishing either claim. The $80/yr permit comes from a TrailChick page updated March 2026; verify with the Tribes. A search summary claimed the Colville Tribes staff the tower periodically, citing a photo entry; no page read confirmed it, so it is left out. Access note in facts is permission per the record. Record fields height_m and status are unchanged (45 ft tower height is not converted because the register does not say whether it runs to the cab floor).
